subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a bundled Slack-plugin action, and what token/privacy/scope contract should govern event-scoped Slack action tokens?
rationale: The request adds workspace-wide search through event-scoped Slack credentials, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent token retention, redaction, API shape, or authorization model.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with ephemeral token handling, read-only action semantics, explicit scope docs, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external plugin/API design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers define a plugin/API seam or external package path that can receive Slack action-token context safely.

options.title: Use legacy user-token search
options.body: Revive a `search.messages` style path only if maintainers explicitly accept that it is not Slack's recommended RTS model and approve the privacy boundary.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` in the Slack plugin with ephemeral token handling, read-only action semantics, explicit scope docs, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across Slack assistant lifecycle, Slack action-parity review, and the close comment that left RTS as the remaining focused path.
